column1: # Belloc's wind-tunnel model: its coefficients measured against angle of attack and sideslip
# Source: H. Belloc, "Wind Tunnel Investigation of a Rigid Paraglider Reference Wing", Journal of
#   Aircraft 52(2), 703-708, 2015, doi:10.2514/1.C032513. Two sets of the same measurements:
#   'figures' - the curves P. F. Heatwole plots in "Parametric Paraglider Modeling" (MSc thesis,
#     2022, Figures 9.7 to 9.12; CC BY 4.0), recovered from the vector paths of his figures
#     path's vertices mapped onto the axes' limits his plotting script sets (NLLT/belloc.py). The
#     'tunnel' rows are his black 'Tunnel' line, Belloc's data; the 'AVL', 'XFLR5' and 'NLLT' rows
#     are his three models of the same wing (AVL 3.36, XFLR5 6.47 inviscid, glidersim's Phillips
#     lifting line on XFOIL polars), kept for the slopes they compare at.
#   'fairaero' - CL and CD against the angle with no sideslip as github.com/fairaero/Belloc-validation-data
# measure: measured (Belloc's balance); 'figures' digitised from vector paths, to the plot's own
#   precision; AVL, XFLR5 and NLLT computed by Heatwole
# The two sets are one test with two angles. At equal lift their drag agrees within 0.0012 (2%), and
# the figures' angle (Heatwole's column 'Alphac') is the fairaero file's plus 1.70 degrees per unit of
# lift (rms 0.05 degrees): an angle corrected for the load, which deflects the model on its rod or
# turns the flow at the walls. The figures' is the one compared with. Neither is corrected for the
# Coefficients on the reference of belloc-2015-model.tsv: 0.444 m2; Cl, Cm and Cn on 0.350 m, about
# T1. Lift and drag are in the wind's axes; CY, Cl, Cm, Cn in the body's: x forward, y right, z down;
# beta positive with the wind from the right.
# method       tunnel, or one of Heatwole's models
# coefficient  CL, CD, Cm, CY, Cl or Cn
# sweep        alpha or beta: the angle that varies
# angle_deg    the angle that varies, degrees
